title: Baguettes à l'Ancienne (Cold-Retarded Artisan French Baguettes)
originalTitle: Baguettes à l'Ancienne (Cold-Retarded Artisan French Baguettes)
ingredients: 6 cups (765g) unbleached bread flour or French Type 65 flour
2.5 to 2.75 cups (590–650ml) ice-cold water (40–50°F — key to delaying yeast before cold retardation)
instructions: Whisk together flour, salt, and instant yeast. Add the ice-cold water and mix with a stiff spatula or dough whisk until a wet, sticky dough forms; rest 5 minutes, then stretch-and-fold vigorously for 3 minutes.
Transfer to a lightly oiled bowl, cover tightly, and refrigerate immediately (40°F) overnight or up to 4 days for slow enzymatic flavor development.

Two hours before baking, transfer the cold dough to a floured counter to warm up for 90 minutes. Divide into 3–6 pieces, gently pre-shape into cylinders, and roll into 14-inch baguettes without degassing the open crumb.

Preheat oven with a baking stone and steam pan to 500°F (260°C). Score each baguette with 3–5 diagonal slashes, slide onto the stone, pour 1 cup boiling water into the steam pan, and bake at 475°F for 20–24 minutes until blistered and deep golden brown.
sourceTitle: The Fresh Loaf · Peter Reinhart's Baguettes à l'Ancienne
